query: To test whether flies with more accurate head-direction encoding also show narrower EPG bumps under the same visual cue condition, examine the across-fly relationship between HD encoding accuracy and bump width in the first dim-cue block. For each of the 15 flies, use movement periods only. Compute HD encoding accuracy as one minus circular variance of the EPG bump-phase-to-head-direction offset, and compute mean bump width from the same retained time points. Across flies, use Pearson correlation to test the relationship between HD encoding accuracy and mean bump width. Generate a single scatter plot with HD encoding accuracy on the x-axis and bump width on the y-axis, one point per fly, a fitted regression line, and the Pearson P value annotated in the panel. Save the per-fly values, correlation statistics, and figure.

analyse_plan.Objective: Test across-individual correlation between HD encoding accuracy and bump width.
analyse_plan.Validation Checks: Verify data from first dim cue block (200 s); confirm Pearson correlation assumptions. HD encoding accuracy is computed as 1 - circular variance of the EPG bump-phase relative to HD.
analyse_plan.Steps: 1. Load Data: Load the per-fly EPG ΔF/F traces, FicTrac-derived HD time series, and immobility flags for the first 200-s dim-cue block (the block where HD encoding accuracy is most variable across individuals) across the 15 flies. 2. Preprocess Imaging: Apply NoRMCorre rigid x/y/z motion correction to the two-photon volumes (12 z-slices, 5-µm spacing, 9.18 volumes/s, 256×128-pixel PB), draw the PB mask, divide into 25–40 ROIs along a polyline midline, and compute per-ROI ΔF/F with the 10th-percentile fluorescence as baseline F. 3. Fit Bump Profile Per Frame: Fit a von Mises function f(x) = α·exp(κ·cos(x − µ)) + c to each timepoint with nonlinear-least-squares (trust-region); record µ as bump position, and compute bump width = 2·|cos⁻¹[(1/κ)·log((1/2)(exp(κ) + exp(-κ)))]| from the fit. 4. Apply Quality Filtering: Discard timepoints with adjusted R² < 0.5 from the bump-width and HD-encoding-accuracy computation, and discard timepoints flagged as immobile. 5. Compute Per-Fly Metrics: For each fly, compute HD encoding accuracy = 1 − circular variance of bump_position − (−HD), and the across-time mean bump width, both restricted to retained timepoints. 6. Run Correlation: Compute the Pearson correlation across the 15 flies between HD encoding accuracy and mean bump width and report the correlation P value. 7. Save Key Results: Save the per-fly HD encoding accuracy and mean bump width values from the dim-cue block and the Pearson correlation statistics used for the panel. 8. Visualization: Generate a scatter plot of bump width (y-axis) versus HD encoding accuracy (x-axis) with one dot per fly, draw the linear regression line, and annotate the figure with the Pearson correlation P value (P = 0.01).

key_analysis_results: Significant negative correlation between HD encoding accuracy and bump width (P = 0.01, Pearson, n = 15 flies, dim cue, first block).
key_analysis_conclusions: Different individuals experience the same cue as conveying different information, producing correlated variations in bump width and encoding accuracy.

summary_report.abstract: Individual variation in encoding accuracy tested for correlation with bump width.
summary_report.methods: 15 flies, first dim cue block, Pearson correlation.
summary_report.discussion: Bump width reliably indicates cue informativeness at individual level.
